pairs.subject: page-load-pipeline
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/console.css:7 The stale banner appears only when a read fails, after the first render, in an unreserved `auto` grid row between the top bar and the stage, so the layer the owner is reading is pushed down by content they never asked for, where the standard calls for a reserved slot or an overlay.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/StaleBanner.tsx:34 The banner is in normal flow in grid row 2 (console.css:11, an `auto` row); its live-region wrapper is empty and takes no room until a read fails, so the banner is inserted above the reader rather than overlaid or reserved.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/Console.tsx:211 Every non-first-paint layer is its own lazyPart chunk (layers.tsx:72, Console.tsx:57) and is preloaded on idle after first paint; the first-paint centre and waiting layers stay in the first load.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/layers/core.tsx:2 Tauri packaged shell loading from disk, which the technique excludes; the first-paint layers ship in the entry bundle anyway, not discovered late.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/Console.tsx:182 A single-document app with hash routing and its own history stack; navigations never leave the document, and the console folder has no unload/pagehide/pageshow handler.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/perf.test.tsx:21 A packaged shell launch is not a document navigation (the technique excludes it); the context's own gates are lab counts of DOM nodes and reads, which is boot or mount territory.

pairs.registryProposal: layout-stability-by-reservation's 'never insert above the reader' is written for public documents; it should say whether an error or stale banner in a desktop shell (late, unrequested, but safety-relevant) should overlay or reserve a slot, since 'appears only on a user action' does not cover a failure notice.
